display.purpose: Hero identity and primary first-viewport statement.

shadows.name: chat-overlay
shadows.purpose: Separates the utility chat overlay from the page.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Subtle hover, color, and visibility transitions.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Outlined mint action for contact and section progression.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: transparent; color: #64ffda; border: 1px solid #64ffda; padding: 0.75rem 1.5rem; border-radius: 4px; font: 500 1rem Inter, sans-serif; transition: all 0.3s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: rgba(100,255,218,0.1); transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #64ffda; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Console Card
components.description: Bordered surface for services and project evidence.
components.css: .ds-card { background: rgb(15,20,35); color: #f0f0f0; border: 1px solid rgb(30,40,60); border-radius: 8px; padding: 2rem; transition: transform 0.3s ease, border-color 0.3s ease; } .ds-card:hover { transform: translateY(-3px); border-color: #64ffda; }

components.name: Skill Chip
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-block; background: rgb(15,20,35); color: #f0f0f0; border: 1px solid rgb(30,40,60); border-radius: 20px; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; font: 500 0.9rem Inter, sans-serif; } .ds-chip:hover { border-color: #64ffda; transform: translateY(-2px); }

components.name: Primary Navigation
components.description: Fixed, quiet section navigation with mint hover signal.
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; gap: 2rem; background: rgb(3,7,18); padding: 1rem; } .ds-nav a { color: #f0f0f0; text-decoration: none; font: 500 1rem Inter, sans-serif; transition: color 0.3s ease; } .ds-nav a:hover, .ds-nav a:focus-visible { color: #64ffda; }

narrative.overview:
The visual system reads like a precise operational console for senior engineering judgment: dark, stable, low-noise, and lit by rare mint signal. It should feel technically fluent without slipping into sci-fi decoration. The interface gives evidence room to breathe, using calm structure, bordered surfaces, and measured motion to make Shaun's experience feel trustworthy and current.

The system is restrained by default. Cards, timelines, chips, and contact surfaces sit on tonal navy layers rather than heavy ornament. Signal Mint marks identity, wayfinding, interactive affordance, and proof points; it should feel like live telemetry on an otherwise quiet infrastructure plane.
keyCharacteristics: Dark technical canvas with layered navy surfaces.
Mint accent used as signal, not decoration.
Inter/system typography with direct hierarchy and practical rhythm.
Flat cards, thin borders, rounded corners, and subtle hover lift.
Professional, outcome-oriented copy presentation with minimal flourish.

rules.name: The Signal Rarity Rule
rules.body: Mint is a status signal and wayfinding device; do not flood large backgrounds with it or turn every element into an accent block.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Static cards and sections should not gain heavy shadows. Reserve shadows for media, overlays, and purposeful hover states.

dos: Do treat Signal Mint as a rare operational signal for identity, navigation, action, and proof.
Do preserve the dark navy layered hierarchy when adding sections or components.
Do use thin borders, small radii, and subtle hover lift for interactive confidence.
donts: Don't introduce unrelated bright accent hues unless a redesign explicitly replaces the visual world.
Don't add heavy shadows, glassmorphism, neon glows, or decorative gradients to ordinary cards.
Don't swap in playful, serif, handwritten, or novelty typography for the core interface.
